items.comparator: Researchers’ estimated time to create the knowledge base without the AI workflow; no independent or controlled comparison stated.
items.quantitative_outcome: A Saint-Gobain program manager said: “Without using this technology, it would have taken our researchers a year to create the knowledge base. Using AI, it took us a couple of hours.” The team assembled 62,000 patents and 44,000 abstracts and developed hypotheses about cement-additive ingredients for testing in about six weeks.
items.signal: AI-assisted literature and patent synthesis for cement-additive research; the scale of the assembled knowledge base may be a distinctive workflow asset, but no measured discovery or product outcome is reported yet.
items.source: Microsoft reported the account and quoted Saint-Gobain’s digital acceleration program manager.

items.comparator: Compared with the prior process; the article does not specify the test setup or sample size.
items.quantitative_outcome: Waters says Peak Integration can “reduce manual interventions by 95%,” “improves testing accuracy by 76%,” and “is 50% faster than the prior process.”
items.signal: AI/ML-assisted chromatographic peak integration for pharmaceutical quality testing, with reported reductions in manual work and gains in accuracy and speed. This is a weak signal: the reported gains are notable, but the article attributes them to Waters and does not provide independent validation or detailed measurement methods.

A collaboration with Oracle and Abu Dhabi healthcare company M42 will combine AstraZeneca’s scientific, clinical-development and regulatory expertise with Oracle’s real-world data, cloud infrastructure and AI-enabled clinical capabilities. The initial program is intended to identify patients with uncontrolled hypertension, support care and improve clinical-trial recruitment. This is a potential distinctive data-access and workflow signal, but the announcement describes an exploratory collaboration and reports no measured outcome.

Boehringer Ingelheim and Microsoft will investigate AI-based digital patient twins for clinical development, using clinical and other relevant data to explore disease and outcome modelling and trial simulation, including possible synthetic or hybrid control arms. The potential access to and use of relevant data could become distinctive, but the companies say the work is exploratory; no specific dataset or measured benefit is reported.

items.comparator: Compared with requests served using large, general-purpose models; the separate customer-service experiment compared costs before and after, but the source gives no baseline details.
items.quantitative_outcome: The article reports that Santander said selected experiments cost about €0.03 per request with smaller, specialized models, compared with roughly €5 using large, general-purpose models. It also reports a separate customer-service experiment where costs fell by more than 50% as conversation quality improved. Santander described both results as experimental.
items.signal: Experimental evidence of sharply lower AI serving costs, with performance reportedly remaining strong; potentially useful operating advantage, but not evidence of a durable competitive edge yet.

items.comparator: A proof of concept; the article does not identify a specific before-and-after baseline for the reported processing-time reduction. Report completeness was measured against a predefined checklist.
items.quantitative_outcome: The article says banks have achieved “a more than 40 percent reduction in human processing time” in transaction-monitoring investigations. It describes Commerzbank’s work as a proof of concept, but does not attribute that specific percentage to Commerzbank. For the proof of concept, it says agents reviewed histories including customers with more than 15,000 transactions in the analysis window.
items.signal: Potentially material compliance-workflow efficiency and more comprehensive investigation, but the quantified industry result is not specifically tied to Commerzbank and the company example is a proof of concept.
items.source: McKinsey, drawing on banking deployments and describing a Commerzbank proof of concept

items.comparator: Efficiency gains are reported across process stages, but no explicit comparator or measurement method is stated in the available source summary.
items.quantitative_outcome: The customer story reports that the legal solution executes “more than 2 million tasks per month on more than 90 million documents,” with “efficiency gains of 20% to 80%” in stages of the department’s processes.
items.signal: High-volume AI use on a large document corpus with reported process-efficiency gains; the scale and bank-context data may be relevant, though the source summary does not establish that the data are proprietary or explain the measurement baseline.

items.comparator: Sophos’s previous average investigation time of approximately 38 minutes
items.quantitative_outcome: OpenAI reports: “Reduced the average response time for cases using agents from approximately 38 minutes to 89 seconds.” It also reports that AI resolved 52% of MDR cases end-to-end. The article describes the reduction as 96%.
items.signal: Sophos used OpenAI models through the Daybreak programme to accelerate threat investigation. The reported time reduction is a weak signal of operational advantage; the article does not establish whether the outcome is independently evaluated or difficult for competitors to replicate.
items.source: OpenAI, “Sophos cuts threat investigation time by 96% with OpenAI Daybreak”

items.comparator: Average performance across 13 cybersecurity tasks; no separate baseline or competitor comparison stated in the article
items.quantitative_outcome: Dark Reading reports the MiST model “improved average performance across 13 cybersecurity tasks.” The article says it was trained on 220,000 vulnerability records, threat-intelligence reports, detection rules, and other cybersecurity documents; it does not state the size of the improvement.
items.signal: The reported use of a sizable, cybersecurity-focused training corpus and task-level improvement is a weak signal of distinctive data access and capability. The source gives no numeric improvement, so the magnitude cannot be assessed.
items.source: Dark Reading, “So Many AI Security Benchmarks, But None Tell the Whole Story”

items.comparator: Compared with the same uplink channel-estimation functionality without the tested AI-based approach; the source does not give a more detailed baseline or protocol.
items.quantitative_outcome: “Initial lab measurements of AI-based uplink channel estimation demonstrated typical throughput improvements of 10–15%.” The companies also state that measurements in their Bonn and Oulu labs showed uplink throughput improvements of 10–15%.
items.signal: AI-based uplink channel estimation produced a reported throughput gain in lab tests, with field validation still planned. This is a preliminary operating-benefit signal, not evidence yet of a durable competitive advantage.
items.source: Deutsche Telekom, in a joint announcement with Nokia

items.comparator: Customer equipment-related incidents before deployment; the source does not specify the comparison period or methodology.
items.quantitative_outcome: “25% reduction in customer equipment-related incidents” since deployment in April, according to the operator as reported by TelecomTV.
items.signal: AI-based fibre-network predictions are being used to anticipate likely customer outages and intervene proactively. The reported incident reduction is a measurable operating signal, though the report does not provide a baseline period or independent verification.

Expanded collaboration connects Hitachi Energy’s business-system and operational data through a Celonis Context Model to support AI agents that can identify supply risks and recommend actions. This is a distinctive data-and-process integration move, but the announcement reports no measured operating outcome.
